newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA LOOKS AT ENDING 20 PERCENT TAKEOVER LAW.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA LOOKS AT ENDING 20 PERCENT TAKEOVER LAW.

text.p: The Australian government was looking at scrapping a requirement that corporate raiders launch a formal takeover bid before they can hold more than 20 percent of a company's stock, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.
But the spokesman for Ian Campbell, the treasurer's parliamentary secretary, said the plan remained only one of several proposed alterations to the corporations law.

"Until that position paper is out, I can confirm that it's an option that's being examined but we're not giving any great weight to any particular proposal until legislation is framed," the spokesman told Reuters.

He said the government would release several position papers over the next six to eight weeks, outlining proposed reforms in various areas including takeovers, directors' duties and electronic commerce.
The proposals would be based on extensive consultations with the business community over the last two months and draft legislation was expected by the end of 1997, he said.
"It hasn't been bedded down in terms of prescriptive framework," the spokesman said.
"But the feedback from the business community has been, by and large, very positive in terms of them supporting us. We hope to use that support as we go forward into legislation."
He said the changes were aimed at boosting investment as well as creating employment and wealth.
